title: Metal Isn't Colder Than Wood #science #physics
description:
Metal isn't colder than wood. Left in the same room, both sit at room temperature. Your hand is warmer (about 34 °C), and aluminium conducts heat over a thousand times better than wood, so your skin loses heat faster and cools more on the metal. That fast cooling is what you feel as cold.

More heat physics: Why microwaves don't heat food from the inside https://youtu.be/ri17BZl0Iq8

Sources
- American Physical Society, PhysicsQuest 2019: Getting Warmer, Getting Colder (aps.org)
- Incropera, DeWitt, Bergman & Lavine, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer (Wiley), Tables A.1 and A.3 (aluminium ≈ 237 W/m·K; woods ≈ 0.1–0.2 W/m·K) and §5.7 (two solids in contact)
- The skin bars in the animation use the contact-temperature formula with typical values; no measured numbers are shown

subtitles: Leave both in one room, and they reach the same temperature.
But your hand is warmer, about 34 °C.
Aluminium conducts heat over a thousand times better than wood.
So your skin cools more, and faster, on the metal.
That fast cooling is what you feel as cold.
